title: Peanuts vs. almonds: nutrition differences

seo.title: Peanuts vs. almonds: protein, fiber and minerals
seo.meta_description: Per 30 g, peanuts provide ~165 calories, 7.0 g protein and 2.4 g fiber; almonds ~175 calories, 6.5 g protein and 3.2 g fiber. Compare minerals too.
seo.search_intent: Compare peanuts and almonds for protein, fiber, fat, calories and minerals

excerpt: Peanuts and almonds are very similar in a realistic serving. At 30 g, raw peanuts provide about 165 calories, 7.0 g protein, 13.0 g fat and 2.4 g fiber; raw almonds about 175 calories, 6.5 g protein, 15.3 g fat and 3.2 g fiber. Peanuts edge ahead in protein, while almonds provide more fiber, calcium and magnesium.
content_html:
A peanut is botanically a legume and an almond is the seed of a drupe, but put 30 g of each on a plate and the nutrition profiles look surprisingly similar. The differences are real, but not nearly as dramatic as the botanical labels suggest.

Compare 30 g of both, raw

Per 30 gPeanutsAlmonds
Calories~165~175
Protein~7.0 g~6.5 g
Fat~13.0 g~15.3 g
Fiber~2.4 g~3.2 g
Magnesium~54 mg~77 mg
Calcium~15 mg~76 mg

Both rows use current USDA Foundation raw-food references and the food-specific energy calculation for a like-for-like comparison.

Protein: a small peanut advantage

Raw peanuts provide about 23.2 g protein/100 g and almonds 21.5 g. In a 30 g handful, the difference is less than 1 g.

Both can contribute protein, but neither becomes the equivalent of a large main-dish protein serving simply because the per-100-g number is high.

Fiber and minerals: almonds

Almonds provide about 10.8 g fiber/100 g versus 8.0 g in peanuts. They also contain much more calcium—about 254 versus 49 mg/100 g—and more magnesium, about 258 versus 180 mg.

Calories are in the same range

Thirty grams lands around 165–175 calories in these references. Claims that one is dramatically more fattening than the other usually disappear when the serving weight is equalized.

Preparation may matter more than the raw difference

Salt, frying oil, honey, sugar coatings or chocolate can shift the final nutrition more than the natural gap between the two foods. Salted oil-roasted peanuts should not be compared with plain raw almonds as if the base ingredient caused every difference.

For simple versions, choose by flavor, price and your target nutrient: slightly more protein from peanuts; more fiber, calcium and magnesium from almonds.

faq.question: Which has more protein, peanuts or almonds?
faq.answer: Peanuts slightly: about 23.2 versus 21.5 g/100 g in the current raw references.

faq.question: Which has more calcium?
faq.answer: Almonds by a wide margin: about 254 versus 49 mg/100 g.

faq.question: Which has more calories?
faq.answer: They are close at equal portions; about 165 versus 175 calories per 30 g in these references.
